QuestionStmt.S: An iron rod is placed parallel to magnetic field intensity 1000 A/m. The magnetic flux through the rod is $3 \times 10^{-4}$ Wb and its cross-sectional area is $1.5 \text{ cm}^2$. The magnetic permeability of rod in Wb/A·m is

Solution.S:
The rod is placed parallel to the magnetic field, so the magnetic flux density $B$ through the rod is:

$$B = \frac{\phi}{A}$$

Given $\phi = 3 \times 10^{-4}$ Wb and area $A = 1.5 \text{ cm}^2$.

Convert area into square metres:

$$1 \text{ cm}^2 = 10^{-4} \text{ m}^2$$

So,

$$A = 1.5 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}^2$$

Now,

$$B = \frac{3 \times 10^{-4}}{1.5 \times 10^{-4}} = 2 \text{ Wb/m}^2$$

We know that $B = \mu H$.

Given magnetic field intensity $H = 1000$ A/m.

So,

$$\mu = \frac{B}{H} = \frac{2}{1000} = 2 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{Wb} \, \text{A}^{-1} \, \text{m}^{-1}$$

Final Answer: $$\boxed{2 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{Wb A}^{-1} \text{m}^{-1}}$$

Hence, the correct option is B.
